bypass_paths.path: The agent calls the Kubernetes API directly with a token of the registered account from its own pod
bypass_paths.evidence: The agent pod check keeps every API-audience token out of the agent pod, and the preflight denies token minting and Secret reads to the registered account; cases K8S-06 and K8S-08

bypass_paths.path: The agent obtains the executor's token by exec into the executor pod or by running a pod as the registered account
bypass_paths.evidence: The preflight denies running pods, exec into pods, and token minting to the registered account; case K8S-08

bypass_paths.path: Identity or impersonation headers sent through the gateway
bypass_paths.evidence: Impersonate-* and X-Remote-* headers are ignored, removed, and never forwarded, and the preflight denies impersonation; case K8S-01

bypass_paths.path: The gateway account's credential or another broader credential used for the downstream request
bypass_paths.evidence: The executor holds only the registered account's projected token and the gateway credential never reaches it; the preflight runs for the gateway account too; cases K8S-07 and K8S-12

bypass_paths.path: A token from another cluster, or a request to another API server
bypass_paths.evidence: Every review and request goes to the pinned API server with the gateway audience; case K8S-03

bypass_paths.path: The PACT endpoints that require native authentication, such as POST /pact/v0.1/requirements
bypass_paths.evidence: They authenticate through the same token review, pod check, and enrollment rules; case K8S-02

bypass_paths.path: Other pods running as the registered account created by principals other than the agent, and token Secrets of the account
bypass_paths.evidence: The gateway cannot inventory every creator of pods or Secrets in the namespace; excluded in unsupported_forms and recorded in residual_limits (open item O4); no negative fixture applies

bypass_paths.path: Node-level access to the tokens of pods on a node, and other users of the cluster acting on the same resources
bypass_paths.evidence: Not agents of this claim and not mediated by the gateway; excluded in unsupported_forms; no negative fixture applies

unsupported_forms: Universal interception of Kubernetes API access (sample I10): only requests through the gateway's routes are claimed
Arbitrary impersonation (sample I10): the executor never impersonates and the preflight denies the verb
Absence of other additive grants from one YAML snippet (sample I10): RBAC is additive, and the preflight checks a finite list at a time
Users other than service accounts, such as OpenID Connect, X.509, static, and webhook token users: only service accounts map to a workload
Legacy token Secrets, unbound tokens, and offline JWT validation: only reviewed, pod-bound tokens are accepted
Shared service accounts: one registered account per agent, the default of identity-mapping section 5; a workload with more than one enrollment in force is a configuration error (KR-10)
More than one cluster per cluster entry, and namespaces outside the claimed set: cluster and namespace are pinned
Watch, selectors, paging, and every verb other than the get and list of the two rows: the rows send fixed requests only
Authorization through webhooks or modes whose inputs the preflight does not reproduce: the preflight sets no extra, and a webhook can cache decisions

Any field of the I10 profile other than principal_id, namespace, and cluster_id, such as the delegation authority_ref and the runtime isolation evidence: supplied by the deployment outside this profile
Any route other than the two reference routes of protected_routes: not listed, so not claimed
Pods and Secrets of the registered account created by others, node-level access, and other users: excluded by their out_of_claim control in bypass_paths

residual_limits: Post-read: deployment data already returned to the agent is not recalled by a later revocation, and no egress or data-use control is claimed; disclosed here with no bound

Revocation propagation, caller token: no specific mechanism invalidates a TokenRequest token; deleting the pod expires its bound tokens, and a token stays valid until then or until it expires; B = 60 s after deletion (illustrative, probe P3)
Revocation propagation, enrollment: a revocation or compromise mark reaches the gateway within the 0 second status bound of the registry, inside the consistency of the registry backend

Revocation propagation, native permission: a RoleBinding removed after admission takes effect at the API server's next authorization of the executor's request, within the cluster's own authorization consistency (probe P4)
Additive grants between preflights: a grant added after a passing preflight, directly or by ClusterRole aggregation, is not seen until the next preflight, within P + R = 360 s (illustrative)
Finite forbidden list: the preflight checks the listed actions only, and another grant not on the list is not detected
Other pods and Secrets of the registered account: pods that the agent did not create and token Secrets of the account can hold API-audience tokens that the gateway does not see (open item O4)
Preflight inputs: the preflight sets no extra, so an authorizer that decides on extra is not exercised (open item O5)

Token audience: a token minted with both the gateway audience and an API server audience would also be usable against the API server, and the review shows only the intersection with the requested audiences (open item O3)
